sana: Quick heads-up — canary for crescendo-lite-ptq (4-bit asymmetric) shows a cluster of JSON tool-call parse failures right at stream chunk boundaries. Not happening on float32 baseline.

derek: Can you paste a minimal failing log? rough counts?

sana: Failing ~7% of calls for this workload (vs 0.6% baseline). here's a clipped stderr from the runtime postprocess:```
2026-03-22 23:41:12,332 - postprocess - ERROR - json parse error: JSONDecodeError: Expecting ',' delimiter: line 1 column 245 (char 244)
...payload snippet...
{"action": "search", "args": [{"q": "last release notes", "filters": ["releases"]}]}

<<stream continued but truncated>>
```

eli: Looks like truncation near the end — could be streaming chunk size or chunk boundary splitting inside arrays/objects. Is kvcache/prefix length large?

sana: Yes — failures correlate strongly with long conversation prefix + a 3rd-party embed chunk that balloons the context. When prefix < 600 tokens it's fine. With prefix ~1100 tokens failures spike.

grace: Two quick mitigations to try: (1) add a short sentinel after JSON chunk like `
<<END_JSON>>
` so postprocess waits for that token before parsing, (2) wrap output as NDJSON (1 JSON object per line) to make partial-stream reassembly easier.

canary-bot: canary run 7054321000-a completed: baseline (no sentinel) success=93.1% n=2500; sentinel-probe success=99.2% n=2500. (metrics computed on funcall schema compliance only)

ops-bot: Nice delta. We should avoid changing prompt protocols for customers by default. Consider runtime-level conservative fixes: try 1 retry with small suffix repair (+"}}" append heuristics) before emitting parse_error telemetry. Tag requests that get repaired.

derek: I'll open a tiny runtime PR: on parse failure, attempt a single lightweight repair flow — try adding closing braces/brackets, then reparse; if still fails, fall back to returning parse_error. Add a new telemetry tag `parse_rescue_attempted` and `parse_rescue_succeeded`. @sana can you run the 10k eval overnight with that branch and the sentinel variant so we can compare repair vs sentinel?

sana: Yep — kicking off both runs now. will post consolidated numbers tomorrow. quick note: need to ensure repair loop has a strict CPU/time cap so it doesn't amplify p99 latency.

derek: good call. limit to 1 retry + 50ms extra processing budget. also add a rate-limited aggregate metric so we can roll back if repair harms throughput.

eli: If sentinel ends up being consistently better, we can add it to the onboarding guide for PTQ canaries instead of a product change. For the runtime change, pls add an opt-out flag for dedicated/private customers.

grace: FYI, I ran a small synthetic where we injected an intentional stream split in the middle of an array — NDJSON tolerates that much better, but sentinel + repair gives us the highest end-to-end caller success for our structured-output tests.

sana: Thanks all — will post the overnight summary with pass/fail counts and a few example reparations. :thumbsup:

canary-bot: scheduled followup: 7054321000-a-summary -> tomorrow 09:00 PT

ops-bot: note added to runbook: "structured-output: consider sentinel or runtime-repair for quant canaries"

derek: @sana ping me if you see any cases where repair silently changes meaning of args — we should log diffs for manual audit.

sana: will do.
